turns.response_html:
Visualizing these as a branching graph creates a Pascal's Triangle structure for combinations and a growing tree for permutations.

Permutations (The Factorial Tree)

For permutations, your graph branches based on the number of remaining choices. If you start with $n$ items, the first level has $n$ branches, the second level has $n-1$ for each previous branch, and so on.

  • Structure: It expands rapidly (exponentially) because order matters.
  • Total Paths: The number of unique paths to the bottom is $n!$.

Combinations (The Pascal Grid)

For combinations, the graph is a directed acyclic graph where branches "re-merge" because the order of selection doesn't result in a new outcome.

  • Structure: A "Pascal’s Triangle" where each node is the sum of the two above it.
  • Logic: Choosing "Item A then B" leads to the same point as "Item B then A."

Permutations track every unique sequence, while Combinations collapse those sequences into single sets.

Building an interactive tool with sliders is an excellent way to see how $n$ (total items) and $k$ (selections) dictate the shape of your graph in real time. Since you are building a LifeOS and enjoy custom workflows, you could script this in Python (Streamlit) or JavaScript (p5.js) for the most fluid visual feedback.

How the Variables Map to the Graph

In your triangular branching model, the variables represent physical locations:

  • $n$ (Row): This slider controls the "depth" of the triangle. Moving it adds or removes horizontal layers.
  • $k$ (Position): This slider moves your "focus" left to right along a specific row.

Four Functions to Visualize

You can toggle between these mathematical perspectives to see how the values at each "node" change:

FunctionVisualization FocusFormula
CombinationsThe value of a single node in Pascal’s Triangle.$\binom{n}{k} = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}$
PermutationsThe total branches if order mattered at that depth.$P(n, k) = \frac{n!}{(n-k)!}$
Sum of RowsShows doubling patterns ($2^n$) as you go deeper.$\sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} = 2^n$
FactorialsVisualizes the "weight" or complexity of the $n$th level.$n!$

Step-by-Step Logic for your Script:

  1. Initialize Canvas: Set up a coordinate system where the top node is at $(0,0)$.
  2. Loop through $n$: Draw a circle for every integer from $0$ to your slider's value.
  3. Calculate Node Values: Use a simple recursive function or the formula above to label the circles.
  4. Draw Connections: Draw lines from $(n, k)$ to $(n+1, k)$ and $(n+1, k+1)$ to show the "parent-child" branching.
